rules: VLE32FF.V is a unit-stride load instruction that transfers 32-bit elements from memory into a destination vector register group.
If a synchronous exception occurs on element 0, VLE32FF.V takes a trap.
If a synchronous exception occurs on element 0, the vl register is not modified.
If a synchronous exception occurs on an element with an index greater than 0, VLE32FF.V does not take a trap.
If a synchronous exception occurs on an element with an index greater than 0, the vl register is reduced to the index of the element that would have raised the exception.
If the vtype.vma bit is 1, inactive elements in the destination vector register group may be overwritten with 1s.
If the vtype.vta bit is 1, tail elements in the destination vector register group may be overwritten with 1s.
If vstart is greater than or equal to vl, no elements in the destination vector register group are updated.
If vl is 0, no elements in the destination vector register group are updated.
If VLE32FF.V takes a trap due to an interrupt, the vl register is not modified.
If VLE32FF.V takes a trap due to an interrupt, the vstart register is set to a value.
If VLE32FF.V would trigger a debug data-watchpoint trap on an element with an index greater than 0, the vl register is not modified and the debug trap is taken.
If the vm bit is 0, only elements where v0.mask[i] is 1 are active.
VLE32FF.V follows RVWMO at the instruction level.
VLE32FF.V follows RVTSO at the instruction level if the Ztso extension is implemented.
Element operations within VLE32FF.V are unordered.
If the destination vector register group overlaps with the source mask register v0, the encoding of VLE32FF.V is reserved.
Only active elements of VLE32FF.V access memory or raise exceptions.
VLE32FF.V may update active destination elements past the point at which vector length is trimmed.
If an element is not naturally aligned to the size of the element, VLE32FF.V may perform a successful transfer or raise an address-misaligned exception.
